mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as investors shift from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of periods with FEDFUNDS <0.5%, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals labor market deterioration, triggering risk-off flows that produce negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in >60% of UNRATE >5.0% periods, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales growth signal broad demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as recession risks escalate.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >60% of HOUST↓ and RSAFS↓ periods, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During supply chain disruption regimes, declining industrial production signals production bottlenecks that increase inflation and reduce equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of supply chain disruption periods, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly job gains exceeding 100,000 consistently boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >60% of PAYEMS >100k months, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 0.5% signals early monetary tightening, increasing borrowing costs and reducing equity valuations to produce negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >60% of FEDFUNDS >0.5% instances, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production and quarterly GDP growth signal severe supply shocks that increase inflation and erode corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of INDPRO↓ and GDPC1↓ periods, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansion regimes, rising retail sales growth combined with stable housing starts signals robust consumer demand that boosts earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >60% of RSAFS↑ and HOUST stable periods, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 1-year window.
